library.title: Library
library.pageDesc: An instance is three things: a DSH version, a DSH_HOME and a profile. Prepare them here.
library.hostErrorTitle: This host's resources are out of reach
library.hostErrorHint: That is what the machine said. Try again once it is reachable.

home.noProfile: No profile in this instance's DSH_HOME
home.retryHint: Ask that machine about this instance once more.

instances.pageDesc: Each instance binds a DSH version, a DSH_HOME and a profile. Starting one opens DSH's web UI in your browser.
instances.homeHint: The same version can be bound to different DSH_HOMEs, or share one with another instance.
instances.hostScope: A machine's resources are its own: only DSH versions and DSH_HOMEs on {host} can be picked below.
instances.noVersionsDesc: Install one in the Library first, then come back to create an instance.
instances.emptyDesc: Installing a version creates its first instance automatically; you can also add another instance for an installed version here.
instances.deleteContent: Only the launcher's record is removed: the DSH version and the DSH_HOME "{home}" stay. A custom icon for this instance is deleted with it.
instances.deleteHint: Versions and DSH_HOMEs are shared resources; deleting an instance never touches them.
instances.addressHint: A remote instance is reached over this Mac's ssh forward: the remote address is where it runs on its own machine, the local one is where it answers on this Mac (the ports differ when that port was already taken here). 「Open」 uses the local one.
instances.healthNotChecked: Not checked on a remote host
instances.commandCopied: Command copied — paste it into a terminal

homes.deleteBlocked: Still referenced by an instance, cannot be removed
homes.confirmDeleteHome: Remove DSH_HOME "{name}" from the launcher? Only the record is removed; the directory on disk stays.
homes.browserPickHint: The browser preview cannot open a directory picker; type the path instead
homes.remoteAddNote: This is a path on that machine: the launcher creates it there if it is missing and only records it once that machine says it is usable.
homes.confirmDeleteRemoteHome: Remove DSH_HOME "{name}" from the launcher? Only the record goes: the directory on that machine is left exactly as it is.

profiles.profileDeleteConfirm: Delete profile "{name}"? This cannot be undone.
profiles.noHomeSelected: No DSH_HOME yet — add one on the DSH_HOME tab
profiles.pluginsLiveOnInstances: Patch layers belong to a running instance: expand its card on the board, or open its settings, and press Plugins.

plugins.bundlesEmpty: No manageable patch layers in this profile
plugins.bundlesNoneMine: No patch layers of your own — the group below ships with DSH
plugins.bundleManagedWhy: This layer backs DSH's own plugin manager: it can be switched off, never uninstalled
plugins.bundleRemoveConfirm: Uninstall layer "{name}"? The entries and configuration it brought disappear, and this profile stops depending on the package. A linked local source directory is left alone.
plugins.bundleAppliedRestart: Updated layer "{name}" — restart the instance to apply
plugins.bundleRemovedRestart: Uninstalled layer "{name}" — restart the instance to apply
plugins.bundleOrderHint: Order is priority: layers apply top to bottom. A re-mounted layer moves to the end.
plugins.offlineEmpty: This profile holds no patch layers yet
plugins.offlineNote: Read from the profile's own declared layers and dependencies: a read-only projection without the instance's live state, availability, removal rules or row counts. Start the instance to manage them here.
plugins.outcomeOverridden: Overridden by a higher-priority layer; this change has no effect
plugins.outcomeUnknown: The instance returned an unknown result: {application}
plugins.restartNeeded: Layer changes apply after the instance restarts

versions.binMissingHint: This version has no launcher file; it needs installing again.
versions.confirmDeleteVersion: Delete version {version}? Its instances are removed too, and its dedicated DSH_HOME "{path}" is deleted — it holds session history and credentials and cannot be recovered.
versions.confirmInstallContent: Download and install DSH {version} on 「{host}」? An instance and its dedicated directory are created on that machine when it finishes.
versions.confirmInstallSourceContent: Install DSH {version} on 「{host}」? It is published on GitHub only, so it is cloned and built from source on that machine (this can take a while). An instance and its dedicated directory are created when it finishes.
versions.installCancelled: Cancelled; the install process on that machine was stopped

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: How the launcher itself behaves. DSH versions, DSH_HOMEs and profiles live in the Library.

hosts.title: Hosts
hosts.note: The machines the launcher manages. 本机 is the Mac the launcher runs on; it is built in and cannot be removed. A remote host is reached through the system ssh, passwordless only (key or ssh-agent) — the launcher stores no password and no passphrase.
hosts.name: Name
hosts.targetRequired: Fill in an ssh target: an alias from ~/.ssh/config, or a string such as user{'@'}host
hosts.targetHint: Handed to the system ssh as typed: an alias from ~/.ssh/config, user{'@'}host, or user{'@'}host -p 2222.
hosts.registryHint: Only when this host has a registry of its own.
hosts.extraEnvHint: Injected into installs and instances on this host.
hosts.extraEnvInvalid: Environment variables take one KEY=VALUE per line
hosts.dataDirHint: Where this host keeps its versions, dedicated DSH_HOMEs, logs and running record. Empty derives it from that machine's home directory (~/.local/share/dsh-launcher).
hosts.dataDirMissing: not there yet (the launcher creates it on first write)
hosts.cannotReach: A host that cannot be reached is still saved: it may simply be off or off-network right now.
hosts.deleteWarning: This deletes the launcher's record only: nothing on the server is touched, and the instances running there keep running.
hosts.deleteRecords: The versions, DSH_HOMEs and instance records filed under this host go with it, and its instances will no longer show up in the launcher.
hosts.deleteLeft: The remote data directory stays on that machine as it is (versions, dedicated DSH_HOMEs, logs, running record). To look at it yourself, run in a terminal:
hosts.deleteRunning: “{names}” keep running on that machine and the launcher will no longer see them; stopping them has to happen there.

settings.minimizeToTray: Minimize to the tray when the main window closes

terminal.label: External terminal
terminal.hint: An instance's "Open terminal" button uses this terminal, injecting DSH_HOME and the instance's environment.

logLevel.label: Log level
logLevel.hint: Runtime logs go to logs/latest.log in the data directory; each start rotates the previous file.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.back: Go back (inside a field it only blurs)
shortcuts.note: ⌘ on macOS, Ctrl on Windows / Linux. ⌘/Ctrl+R refreshes app state and does not reload the page. Plain typing in a field is never hijacked. Rows marked 'native' are handled by the OS menu.

proxy.title: Proxy
proxy.enabledHint: The launcher's own requests (version downloads, update checks) go through this proxy.
proxy.noProxyHint: Comma-separated hosts / addresses that skip the proxy.
proxy.applyDshHint: Injects HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY / NO_PROXY when starting an instance, overriding the instance's own variables. Running instances need a restart.

update.title: Launcher update
update.channelHint: The dev channel includes pre-releases; the release channel only checks stable versions.

dataDir.title: Data directory
dataDir.desc: The launcher's own data: configuration, logs, installed versions and dedicated DSH_HOMEs all live here.

environment.title: Environment
environment.desc: The toolchain the launcher found and bound. Instances and plugin management use these paths.

instanceEdit.name: Instance name
instanceEdit.defaultProfileHint: Tied to the DSH_HOME above: confirm it again after switching.
instanceEdit.envDesc: Runtime variables injected when the instance starts, overriding same-named system variables. DSH_HOME is injected by the launcher and cannot be overridden.
instanceEdit.envKeyReserved: DSH_HOME is managed by the launcher
instanceEdit.portHint: The port the web UI listens on; empty or out of 1-65535 means a random port. A running instance needs a restart.
instanceEdit.portSavedRandom: Saved; a random port will be used

setup.title: Environment check
setup.desc: Running a DSH instance needs Node.js; installing versions and managing plugins also needs pnpm. The launcher judges by your system environment variables (the PATH your terminal uses) and only searches the usual install directories when they are missing there; if neither has them, you can point it at the executable yourself.
setup.sourceFallback: Not in your system environment variables — found by the launcher in a common install directory
setup.sourceMissing: Not in your system environment variables or the usual install directories
setup.remoteNote: These conclusions come from {host}’s own interactive login shell — the one your terminal on that machine would use — not from this Mac.
setup.skippedUnparsable: {path} reports a version the launcher cannot read ({version}); passed over
setup.nodeCommandDesc: Run this in a terminal to install Node.js:
setup.remoteNodeCommandDesc: Run this in a terminal on this Mac: it connects over ssh and installs Node.js in that machine’s interactive login shell.
setup.pnpmCommandDesc: The launcher needs pnpm {major} or newer. Run this in a terminal to install it:
setup.remotePnpmCommandDesc: That machine needs pnpm {major} or newer. Run this in a terminal on this Mac: it connects over ssh and installs it in that machine’s interactive login shell.
setup.afterInstallHint: Once those commands finish, come back to this window and it re-checks automatically — or use "Re-check" in the header to force a fresh read of your system environment variables.
setup.manualDesc: Choose the {tool} executable yourself, or add it to your PATH in a terminal (for example in ~/.zshrc) and come back to press "Re-check".
setup.manualBroken: The path you picked no longer works; automatic detection is back
setup.overrideApplied: {tool} now uses the file you picked
setup.browserPickHint: The browser preview cannot open a file picker; pick one in the desktop app
setup.remoteManualDesc: A remote host has no file picker here, so type the absolute path on that machine; the launcher checks it by running --version over ssh.

common.copyFailed: Copy failed; select and copy manually
